summary: Summary-figure review, RADiCAL T10 Aug-2026 (all paths under /Users/jameswetzel/Dropbox/01_Research/HEP/RADiCAL/02_Analysis/2026-08_CERN_T10/RADiCAL_TB_T10_Aug-2026). The five-figure set is coherent, honest about caveats, and uses a consistent channel color code (teal=DSB1, red=LuAG, amber=EJ199) — good. Two systemic issues plus two NEW physics findings. SYSTEMIC-1 (major, presentation): the grey annotation/subtitle strips collide with the plot frame in Hero_timing, PulseShapes, all four HowItWorks panels, and ModuleCompare's right y-title — text renders struck-through by the frame line and is barely legible; this is almost certainly a header y-position bug in macros/radStyle.h and one fix repairs every figure. SYSTEMIC-2 (major, staleness): the index page hosting these figures contradicts its own figures — the What-we-tested table (build_site.py:260) says EJ199 = runs 39-41, '+1/+3/+5 done; negative points next', yet PulseShapes is built from run 42 (-7 GeV EJ199), the diagonal-difference table (lines 278-280) lists EJ199 at 5/7/9 GeV, and ModuleCompare plots EJ199 at 1-11 GeV; registry says runs 39-44. Also chip '~300k events' (line 244) vs table sum ~458k vs registry ~700k; pill 'two modules fully analyzed' (246) while every figure carries three channels; header 'Aug 27-30' (243) vs campaign Aug 27-31. NEW PHYSICS FINDING A (major): the DSB1 trend constant term 79 ps (hard-coded in macros/ModuleCompare.C:42) is BELOW the independently validated, energy-independent 107-114 ps reference jitter that is included in every plotted point — physically impossible if the reference enters as a pure constant. The stochastic/constant decomposition is degenerate over the 1-9 GeV lever arm (fit undershoots the 1 GeV point by ~33 ps), so the caption's headline comparison 'constant term 79 vs 138 ps' (build_site.py:266) sells a fit artifact as a physical floor; compare measured points or ref-subtracted estimates instead. The editorial choice of quoting unsubtracted resolutions as the headline is nevertheless CORRECT: DiagDiff is invalidated for DSB1 by the correlated-capillary discovery, and quadrature-subtracting 110 ps from 133 ps is razor-sensitive (ref 105->82 ps intrinsic, ref 114->68 ps), so 133 ps included-ref is the only robust headline. NEW PHYSICS FINDING B (major): all three fitted pulse tails (4.9/6.5/12.5 ns, fitted 8-45 ns after peak per macros/PulseShapes.C:51) are far shorter than BOTH the LYSO:Ce 40 ns tile decay AND LuAG:Ce's own ~60 ns Ce decay, and only 16-32% of light arrives after 8 ns where tile-light dominance would predict a majority. Combined with the response-per-MIP table (0.42 LuAG / 0.32 EJ199 / 1.48 DSB1 MIP-sums per GeV, build_site.py:314), this argues the LuAG and EJ199 shower signals are dominated by direct in-shower excitation of the capillary, not collected tile light — in tension with the site's core 'light-collection channel' framing (line 255) — while DSB1's 4x-larger response-per-MIP with the FASTEST tail points to a prompt extra source (Cherenkov in glass?) rather than waveshifted 40 ns LYSO light, which could not be faster than its source. Alternative: heavy AC-coupling/differentiation in the HG path (undershoot is visible in PulseShapes and HowItWorks panel 2) shortens all tails; the slow LG shapes in HowItWorks panel 3 (rise ~40-50 ns) may in fact be where the LYSO 40 ns light lives — comparing LG-path mean shapes across the three channels is a decisive, already-recorded test. Either way the caption's phrase 'LuAG's scintillation tail' (line 325) mislabels an electronics-convolved effective tail. ModuleCompare caption has minor numeric overreach (details in plot entry); Tertiary11's E-equivalent argument survives the gain-ladder interrogation but should lean on shower-max migration and quote DSB1's 8.0 as a lower bound. EJ199's largest MIP sum is fully consistent with the response ordering once direct-excitation light (MIP) is separated from collected tile light (shower response) — and mildly supports the contaminant hypothesis without proving it, since any PVT-based capillary scintillates brightly under direct ionization; the 6.5 ns tail and the planned dark-pulse photoelectron scale are the real discriminants.

plots.figure: Output/summary/Hero_timing.png (caption: build_site.py:264-269; trend curves hard-coded in macros/ModuleCompare.C:41-42)
plots.what_it_shows: Shower-time resolution sigma_t vs beam energy 1-11 GeV for DSB1 (teal circles, solid fit 323/sqrt(E) (+) 79 ps) and LuAG (red squares, dashed fit 389/sqrt(E) (+) 138 ps), median 4-capillary combination, MCP+DRS reference jitter included. Open markers at 11 GeV flag the purity caveat. Readable points: DSB1 ~366/202/156/141/133 ps at 1/3/5/7/9 GeV, open ~181 at 11; LuAG ~413/274/228/192/190, open ~227.
plots.caption_issues: Numbers check out: 133+/-5 at 9 GeV and 156+/-8 at 5 GeV are visible; constant terms are in the legend; conventions stated both in caption ('Median 4-capillary combination; no reference subtraction') and in the grey strip ('reference included, unsubtracted; open points: e- purity uncertain above ~10 GeV/c'). One substantive issue (major, NEW): the caption's framing 'the trend's constant term is 79 ps vs LuAG's 138 ps' presents fit parameters as physical floors, but 79 ps < the validated 107-114 ps included reference jitter — impossible for a constant reference term. The decomposition is degenerate (fit misses the 1 GeV DSB1 point by ~33 ps low; a fit constrained to constant >= 110 ps would describe 3-9 GeV equally well with a smaller stochastic term). Recommend rewording to compare measured points, or adding one clause noting the constant term is a fit descriptor, not a floor.
plots.design_issues: Major: grey subtitle strip collides with the top frame line — struck-through, barely legible (radStyle header placement; same defect campaign-wide). Minor: legend entries widely spaced with dead vertical space; fit curves start at ~0.75 GeV while the axis starts at 0, leaving an unexplained gap; open-marker convention decipherable only from the semi-legible grey strip. Nit: y-title reads 'shower-time resolution sigma_t [ps]' with awkward split at the top.
plots.physics_questions: (1) Is quoting unsubtracted resolution the right headline? YES — defensible and correct: DiagDiff sigma(diff)/2 is invalidated for DSB1 by the discovered correlated per-capillary terms, and quadrature subtraction 133(+/-5) (-) 110 ps is hypersensitive (d_intrinsic/d_ref ~ 1.5: ref=105 -> 82 ps, ref=114 -> 68 ps), so the ~75 ps DSB1 intrinsic at 9 GeV is a projection, not a headline. The page already does the right thing by placing the intrinsic card directly below. (2) Why does the two-parameter model fail at 1 GeV for DSB1 (366 measured vs 333 fitted) — missing noise/E term, residual daytime-noise in runs 37/38, or 1 GeV shower-containment fluctuations? Adding an N/E term would push the fitted constant even lower, underscoring that it is unphysical. (3) The common reference means the cross-channel RANKING of constant terms is still fair — but the difference 138 vs 79 should then be quoted as intrinsic-constant difference after removing the common 110 ps in quadrature: LuAG sqrt(138^2-110^2)=83 ps vs DSB1 ~0 (unresolvable) — a much stronger statement that the caption leaves on the table.

plots.figure: Output/summary/ModuleCompare.png (caption: build_site.py:302-309; macro macros/ModuleCompare.C, EJ199 trend 1218/sqrt(E) hard-coded at line 71)
plots.what_it_shows: Left: sigma_t vs E, log-y, all three channels; EJ199 labeled 'photostatistics-limited (no stable trend)' with points ~1300/640/405/349/303 ps at 1/3/5/7/9 GeV, open ~470 at 11. Right: Sum-LG peak vs E: DSB1 ~3750/6700/9000/9900 ADC-eq at 3/5/7/9 GeV (open ~10700 at 11), LuAG ~1700/2950/4800/5800 (open ~5700), EJ199 ~1300/2700/4650/5700, 11 GeV omitted ('fit unstable').
plots.caption_issues: Three numeric overreaches (all minor individually, but they are the caption's quantitative content): (a) 'delivers ~2.1x the light (~1,250-1,390 vs ~660 ADC-eq/GeV)' — the plotted ratio is 2.2 at 3 GeV, 2.27 at 5, but 1.9 at 7 and 1.7 at 9; and the DSB1 9 GeV point gives ~1,100/GeV, outside the quoted 1,250-1,390 range (the range silently excludes the daytime-noise 9 GeV run without saying so). (b) '~660' here vs '~620' in the adjacent table (build_site.py:312) — same page, two LuAG response numbers. (c) 'runs ~2x slower than LuAG at every point' — the point-by-point ratio is 3.1x at 1 GeV, 2.3x at 3, 1.6x at 5/7, 1.4x at 9; '~2x on average, converging at high E' would be accurate and more interesting (it hints the EJ199 deficit is stochastic, as the photostatistics label claims). Conventions properly stated: log scaling declared, open-marker caveat declared, EJ199 11 GeV omission declared on-plot.
plots.design_issues: Major: right-panel y-title 'Sum-LG,peak [ADC-eq]' collides with the frame/tick region (struck-through). Minor: right panel has no fit/trend lines so 'response linearity ... established' in the caption is asserted rather than shown (a per-GeV normalized panel or trend line would carry it); DSB1/LuAG have no data below 3 GeV on the right panel and the caption does not say why (1 GeV response points exist for timing). Nit: '~2.1x the light' lives inside the legend — data claims in legends are easy to miss when figures are reused.
plots.physics_questions: (1) THE ASKED CHECK — is EJ199's largest MIP sum (~1,850 vs LuAG 1,480 vs DSB1 920, table at build_site.py:313) consistent with the response ordering? YES, once light sources are separated: the MIP sum measures direct ionization scintillation in the capillary (PVT-based plastic: ~10k ph/MeV at high optical quality beats LuAG's higher dE/dx with poorer fiber trapping/535 nm emission, and easily beats low-yield Ce glass), while shower response adds collected tile light on top. EJ199 having the largest MIP signal but the SMALLEST response-per-MIP (0.32 vs LuAG 0.42 vs DSB1 1.48) is exactly the signature of a channel with strong direct excitation and near-zero tile-light collection — consistent with the spec mismatch AND with the ordering. Caveat: a bright direct-MIP signal is expected for any PVT capillary, contaminant or not, so this row supports but cannot prove the contaminant hypothesis; the 6.5 ns tail and the planned dark-pulse p.e. calibration are the discriminants. (2) The near-equality LuAG 0.42 vs EJ199 0.32 response-per-MIP suggests BOTH channels' shower response is dominated by direct in-shower capillary excitation (response-per-MIP ~ geometric MIP-crossings/GeV), quietly undermining the 'light-collection channel' framing for these two — worth an explicit statement. (3) EJ199 'photostatistics-limited' with LuAG-comparable ADC response but ~2x worse timing implies ADC-eq/photon differs by ~4x between the channels (gain ladder, PDE at different emission wavelengths) or the EJ199 light is time-dispersed — quantifiable only after the photoelectron scale; flag that the timing comparison is currently in detected-charge units, not photons. (4) The DSB1/LuAG ratio falling from 2.3 to 1.7 with E: LG-ceiling compression of DSB1 at high E, or the gain ladder? Same mechanism as the retired saturation — a pointer to the forensics would inoculate readers.

plots.figure: Output/summary/PulseShapes.png (caption: build_site.py:323-326; macro macros/PulseShapes.C — expo tail fit over 8-45 ns after peak at line 51, tail fraction = area>8ns/total at lines 54-57, 10-90 rise at line 46)
plots.what_it_shows: Mean tagged-electron pulse shapes, peak-aligned and peak-normalized, same -7 GeV beam, runs 27 (LuAG) / 33 (DSB1) / 42 (EJ199). Legend: DSB1 tail tau=5 ns, 16% of light after 8 ns; LuAG tau=12 ns, 32%; EJ199 tau=6 ns, 25%. Rising edges overlap; DSB1 undershoots below zero ~25-35 ns; LuAG persists to ~60 ns.
plots.caption_issues: Minor: caption quotes 4.9/6.5/12.5 ns while the on-plot legend prints rounded 5/6/12 (%.0f in PulseShapes.C:80-82) — the extra digits are not visible or derivable from the figure; print one decimal in the legend or round the caption. Minor: 'identical readout-limited 4.4 ns rise' — 4.4 appears nowhere on the plot (it comes from the macro's printf) and 'readout-limited' is an interpretation, not a measurement shown. Major (interpretive, NEW): 'LuAG's scintillation tail (tau ~ 12.5 ns)' mislabels the observable — LuAG:Ce's intrinsic Ce decay is ~60 ns and LYSO:Ce's is ~40 ns; 12.5 ns matches neither, so what is fitted (over 8-45 ns, well past the electronics core) is an effective, electronics-convolved pulse tail. The cross-channel RANKING and the 'less late light -> smaller constant term' logic survive; the physical attribution does not. The EJ199-between-DSB1-and-LuAG fingerprint framing is fine.
plots.design_issues: Major: grey header strip struck through by the frame. Minor: curves dip visibly below zero (AC-coupling/pole-zero undershoot) with no mention in caption or on plot — yet this undershoot is material to interpreting the tail numbers; annotate it. Minor: x-axis runs to ~78 ns but all curves end by 60 ns — dead right third. Nit: 'per material' in the alt-text vs 'by capillary channel' in the title.
plots.physics_questions: (1) THE ASKED CHECK — are 4.9-12.5 ns tails consistent with LYSO:Ce 40 ns being the light source? NO, and this is the sharpest physics tension in the summary set. A collection/WLS channel cannot emit faster than its 40 ns source; a 40 ns component present at meaningful amplitude would dominate an expo fit over 8-45 ns and push the after-8ns fractions far above the observed 16-32%. So either (a) the dominant light in ALL three channels is prompt direct in-shower excitation (+Cherenkov) of the capillary itself — consistent with the response-per-MIP table for LuAG/EJ199 — or (b) the HG readout chain differentiates the slow component away (the visible undershoot is evidence of AC-shaping), hiding the tile light. (2) Decisive test already in the data: HowItWorks panel 3 shows the LG-path waveforms rising over ~40-50 ns — if the LG shape carries the scintillation input, the LYSO 40 ns component should appear there; overlay LG-path mean shapes for runs 27/33/42 and see whether they are channel-independent (tile light) or channel-ordered (direct light). (3) DSB1 paradox: 4x the response-per-MIP (i.e., a large non-direct light source) yet the FASTEST tail — waveshifted 40 ns tile light cannot be prompt, so is the extra source Cherenkov in the glass fiber, and if so does that explain both the timing superiority and the (photostat-favorable) high response? A prompt-fraction estimate from these very shapes would test it. (4) Even LuAG's 12.5 ns is 5x shorter than LuAG:Ce's own ~60 ns decay — quantify the shaper time constant from the undershoot and deconvolve before quoting any tau as material physics.

plots.what_it_shows: Four-panel annotated walkthrough of one measurement, mean waveforms of 704 tagged +5 GeV electrons from LuAG run 15: (1) both XCET Cherenkov counters fire (XCET040 teal ~264 ADC-eq peak at ~90 ns, XCET043 blue ~222 at ~84 ns); (2) MCP reference pulse (~580 peak); (3) four LG capillary waveforms, slow shapes peaking ~660-810 at ~70-80 ns; (4) HG capillary pulse (~1,580 peak) with dashed '15% threshold' line at ~240.
plots.caption_issues: Accurate. Provenance numbers (704 events, run 15, 5 GeV, XCET z-positions 39.7 m / ~45 m) are not on the figure but are legitimate caption-only context. The 15% threshold line is drawn AND labeled and matches 0.15 x 1580 — good. Conventions (median of 4 capillaries, threshold on HG copy at 15% of predicted peak) stated in caption and panel subtitles. Nit: panel 1 shows XCET043 peaking BEFORE XCET040 in record time while the caption orders 040 upstream of 043 — cable/record offsets, but a caption clause ('record times include cable offsets') would prevent the obvious misreading. Nit: panel-2 subtitle '~10 ps reference clock' vs the validated ~105-114 ps total reference budget elsewhere on the page — true of the MCP alone, misleading about the system; say 'MCP (~10 ps device) + DRS inter-group ~ 105 ps system'.
plots.design_issues: Major: grey subtitle strips struck through by frames in all four panels — worst here because these subtitles ARE the pedagogy. Minor: visible discontinuity/glitch in the panel-3 LG waveforms at ~125 ns (DRS4 segment artifact?) — unexplained on a figure whose purpose is pedagogy; either crop the record or footnote it. Minor: panel-3 legend colors (capillary 7 dark blue vs capillary 4 teal) are close under colorblind simulation. Nit: panels 2/4 waste the 100-200 ns half of the record.
plots.physics_questions: (1) NEW cross-figure tension: why are the LG-path shapes (rise ~40-50 ns, peak ~75 ns) so radically slower than the HG copy (peak ~12 ns, few-ns tail) of the SAME SiPM light? If the LG path is deliberately integrated/shaped, say so; if not, the LG shape may be showing the LYSO 40 ns scintillation that the HG path differentiates away — directly feeding the PulseShapes direct-vs-collected question. The site never states the dual-gain shaping difference anywhere I could find. (2) 'summed peak proportional to energy' — is Sum-LG the sum of per-channel peaks or the peak of the summed waveform? With ~5 ns relative-timing spreads these differ; the notation Sum-LG,peak in ModuleCompare inherits the ambiguity. (3) The 15%-of-PREDICTED-peak threshold (predicted from the LG transfer line, per the clipped-pulse recovery) makes the timing immune to HG clipping — worth one caption clause here since this panel is where readers learn the method. (4) XCET peak amplitudes (222/264) at +5 GeV with 9.1% e-purity: are these means over tagged events only? If tagged events include kaon/proton accidental coincidences the mean XCET amplitude is biased — trivial here, but the panel invites the question.

plots.figure: Output/summary/Tertiary11.png (caption: build_site.py:345-353; macro macros/Tertiary11.C — class cut at line 77: SumLG<400=miss, <floorC=partial, else contained; 9 GeV overlay at line 85; E-eq from contained peak vs response curve, lines 98-126)
plots.what_it_shows: Four panels. Top: -11 GeV tagged Sum-LG spectra classed miss/partial/contained with the 9 GeV tagged shape overlaid (scaled): LuAG miss 467 / partial 213 / contained 187, contained E-eq 9.7 GeV, data ending ~8k; DSB1 miss 189 / partial 456 / contained 303, E-eq 8.0 GeV, hard edge ~13.5k (LG ceiling ~13.6k). Bottom: MCP pulse-height distributions (fraction, log-y) for untagged (~97% pi), tagged-miss, tagged-contained — largely overlapping, contained showing a sparse hard tail.
plots.caption_issues: All on-figure numbers check (class counts, E-eq values, overlay). The timing pair '181/227 ps vs 366/412 at 1 GeV' is not on this figure but is derivable from Hero_timing on the same page — acceptable, borderline. Minor: 'DSB1's 8.0 is compressed by its LG ceiling' correctly names the bias but then the number should be quoted as a lower bound ('>= 8.0 GeV'); a clipped spectrum's fitted peak is biased low by construction. Minor: 9.7 vs 11 is -12%, inside +/-15% as claimed — arithmetic fine — but see physics question 1 for why the envelope is the weaker of the two available arguments. Minor: the overlay legend says '9 GeV tags (scaled)' without stating the normalization (scaled to what — contained counts? area in the peak window?); the macro comment (line 85, 'contained region only for shape') suggests shape-matching in the contained window, which the caption should say, since the red dashed curve visibly extends into the low-Sum-LG region where it represents the 9 GeV run's own miss/partial population — the shape agreement claim is contained-vs-contained and the caption should scope it that way.
plots.design_issues: Minor: log-y with 187-467 events over ~100 bins yields single-event spike forests, especially the bottom panels between 1.5-2.5k ADC-eq — coarser binning or markers would let shape agreement be judged by eye instead of asserted. Minor: top-left x-axis runs to 12k with data ending ~8k (dead third). Minor: bottom-panel y-label 'fraction' with normalization per class unstated on the plot. Nit: 'E-eq' never defined on the figure (contained-peak / response-curve, per the macro); a reader outside the site cannot reconstruct it. Nit: the miss-class grey is near-invisible where it overlaps the amber partial class.
plots.physics_questions: (1) THE ASKED CHECK — does the E-equivalent argument survive the gain-ladder systematic? Qualitatively YES, but the caption leans on the weaker crutch. The +/-15% envelope means the 9.7 measurement is really '11 GeV consistent within cross-run gain systematics' — it cannot distinguish 9.7 from 11.2, but it robustly excludes the few-GeV tertiary-electron hypothesis the trial exists to kill, and the timing (181/227 ps, hard-shower-like) plus the 9 GeV shape agreement close the case. Stronger available argument the caption skips: the site's own retired-saturation forensics PREDICTS E-eq below 11 from Longo shower-max migration alone (the fixed sampling depth undersamples deeper 11 GeV showers), so 9.7 is not merely 'inside the envelope' — it is roughly where a genuine 11 GeV electron SHOULD land on a 9 GeV-anchored scale. Citing that converts a defensive statement into a positive consistency check. (2) NEW, unaddressed: the campaign's own beam finding is that electrons pulse SMALLER on the MCP, yet the bottom panels show tagged-contained with a slightly HARDER tail than the ~97%-pi untagged sample, and the caption says 'no species contradiction'. With 187-303 events the excess is statistically soft, but the expected signature was a SOFTER contained distribution — quantify (means or a KS test) rather than assert, and check whether the hard tail is time-walk or a few pile-up events. (3) The class-balance flip between modules (LuAG miss-dominated 467/187, DSB1 partial-dominated 456/303) with the SAME beamline: is the miss/partial boundary (SumLG<400 fixed vs floorC) module-dependent in a way that moves events between classes, or did the halo actually differ between runs 30 and 31? This bears directly on the unexplained-halo caveat. (4) The 467 misses at -11 GeV/c are tagged by BOTH Cherenkovs at 0.06 bar — what halo species radiates there? Soft tertiary electrons scraping the aperture is plausible as stated; a transverse-position handle (relative capillary amplitudes in the partial class) could test it without a tracker.
